headings: Watch every inverter. Invoice every offtaker.
states.bodyTextSample: FOR SOLAR ARRAY OWNERS & OPERATORS Watch every inverter. Invoice every offtaker. Array Operator watches every inverter for you — catching the quiet underperformer the day it slips, drafting the warranty claim when one dies — and turns your utility bills into a solar-credit invoice for every offtaker — the customer who receives a share of your solar credits — drafted and ready to send. One connection. Every panel. No spreadsheets. Start free — connect in 60 seconds → Sign in ✓ 14-day free trial, no card · ✓ Read-only — we only see production data · ✓ Disconnect anytime, purged in 24h PICK WHAT YOU NEED — PAY FOR WHAT YOU USE $0.15 / kW · month fleet monitoring ＋ $20 / offtaker you invoice run either, or both — a 100 kW array ≈ $15/mo monitoring; 3 offtakers ≈ $60/mo invoicing Live monitorin

states.name: 08-resources
states.title: Array Operator — your array, working for you
headings: Know the rules that move your credits.
New England REC market as of 2026-07
states.bodyTextSample: THE VERMONT SOLAR OPERATOR’S BRIEFING Know the rules that move your credits. Net-metering rates, Renewable Energy Credit (REC) market prices, active rate cases, and the regulatory changes that decide what your arrays earn across New England — tracked in one place and refreshed daily, so you never bill on a stale rate or miss a decision that affects your offtakers. YOUR STATE Vermont New Hampshire Maine Massachusetts Connecticut Rhode Island LATEST & LIVE DAILY Updated news Jul 10, 2026 · state/REC data Jul 13, 2026 · 7 updates for Vermont DAILY REFRESH AUG 1, 2026 DEADLINE New net-metering rates take effect August 1 Under the PUC's 2026 biennial order (Case 26-0291-INV), the Category I adjustor drops about 2¢/kWh and the small-solar siting charge rises from 4¢ to 5¢/kWh for systems permitted Aug 1, 2026 through Jul 31, 2028. Existing arrays keep their locked-in rate. Vermont PUC ↗ JUN 1, 2026 ADVOCACY REV: 2026 net-metering cuts will further slow Vermont solar Renewable Energy Vermont's press statement notes applications for systems under 150 kW fell 24% from 2024 to 2025 and argues the PUC should have offset the loss of the federal residential solar tax credit rather than raise th
